{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-chain-vec-order}
#### The order of the factors matters

The vector chain rule (@thm-chain-vec) is like the univariate
[chain rule](calculus.qmd#thm-chain-rule),
but the order matters now:
$\derivf{\vy}{\vx}$ is $p \times q$ and $\derivf{z}{\vy}$ is $q \times 1$,
so the product $\derivf{z}{\vy} \derivf{\vy}{\vx}$ in the other order
is not even defined unless $p = 1$.

The version presented here is for the gradient (@def-vector-derivative), a column vector.
The total derivative (@def-row-vector-derivative), a row vector,
is the transpose of the gradient (@thm-row-deriv-tp-col-deriv),
and transposing both sides gives
$\tp{\paren{\derivf{z}{\vx}}} = \tp{\paren{\derivf{z}{\vy}}} \tp{\paren{\derivf{\vy}{\vx}}}$,
with the factors in the reverse order;
there $\tp{\paren{\derivf{\vy}{\vx}}}$ is the Jacobian matrix of $\vy$ as a function of $\vx$ (@def-jacobian-matrix).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-chain-vec}
#### Applying the vector chain rule

Let $\vx = \tp{(x_1, x_2)}$,
$\vy = \vec{g}(\vx) = \tp{(x_1 + x_2,\ x_1 x_2)}$,
and $z = f(\vy) = y_1^2 + y_2$.
Then

$$
\ba
\underbrace{\derivf{z}{\vx}}_{2 \times 1}
&= \underbrace{\derivf{\vy}{\vx}}_{2 \times 2}
\underbrace{\derivf{z}{\vy}}_{2 \times 1}
&& \text{(vector chain rule)}
\\
&= \sbmat{
1 & x_2 \\
1 & x_1
}
\sbmat{
2y_1 \\
1
}
&& \text{(differentiate } \vec{g} \text{ and } f \text{)}
\\
&= \sbmat{
2(x_1 + x_2) + x_2 \\
2(x_1 + x_2) + x_1
}
&& \text{(multiply, and substitute } y_1 = x_1 + x_2 \text{)}
\\
&= \sbmat{
2x_1 + 3x_2 \\
3x_1 + 2x_2
}
&& \text{(collect terms)}
\ea
$$

This matches differentiating $z$ directly:
$z = (x_1 + x_2)^2 + x_1 x_2 = x_1^2 + 3x_1 x_2 + x_2^2$,
so $\deriv{x_1} z = 2x_1 + 3x_2$ and $\deriv{x_2} z = 3x_1 + 2x_2$.
The product in the other order,
a $2 \times 1$ matrix times a $2 \times 2$ matrix,
is not defined.
The total derivative is the transpose,
the row vector $(2x_1 + 3x_2,\ 3x_1 + 2x_2)$.

:::

::: notes
See <https://quickfem.com/finite-element-analysis/>,
specifically <https://quickfem.com/wp-content/uploads/IFEM.AppF_.pdf>

See also <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient#Relationship_with_Fr%C3%A9chet_derivative>
:::
